title: Canonical common-stage derived cohomology realization and source identification
statement:
Fix a finite-field datum $D=(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $Y_0$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Use the finite intermediate fields [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set] and the actual common-stage constructible Pair category $D^b_c(Y,\Omega)$, $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$ [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Choose a compactification $c_0$ for compact support [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. For $\epsilon\in\{\mathrm{ordinary},\mathrm{compact}\}$, let $C_{E,\epsilon}:D^b_c(Y,E)\to D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)$ be ordinary or compact cohomology followed by the point fibre [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology, def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Realize it in $D(\Omega)$ by the canonical scalar-and-size extension along the actual embedding of the small coefficient model $E$ into $\Omega$ [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport]. Write $R_{E,\epsilon}$ for this functor and $\beta_{K,L}:R_{E,\epsilon}(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}R_{L,\epsilon}(M_L)$ for the specified change-of-coefficients comparison when $K=(E,M)$ and $E\subset L$: the localized whole-system operation mate, point-fibre scalar comparison and balanced tensor tower, with their actual associators. Define $C_{\Omega,\epsilon}:D^b_c(Y,\Omega)\to D(\Omega)$ to be the unique functor with object value $C_{\Omega,\epsilon}(E,M)=R_{E,\epsilon}(M)$ and whose map on a common-stage representative $f:M_L\to N_L$ of $K\to K'$ is
$$\beta_{K',L}^{-1}\circ R_{L,\epsilon}(f)\circ\beta_{K,L}.$$
The source identification is the specified equality $C_{\Omega,\epsilon}(E,M)=R_{E,\epsilon}(M)$ from this defining object formula. Equality and composition of representatives are those of the actual common-stage category, including identity enlargements. The scheme universe $u$ and coefficient-closure universe $v$ are independent; the realized target is the standard $D(\operatorname{ModuleCat}^{\max(u,v)}\Omega)$. This defines the canonical cohomology functor and its source equality, without asserting invertibility of Frobenius transport.
